timeline.title: ITS Incom
timeline.desc: Trained as a cloud developer: full-stack apps with ASP.NET and Angular or Flutter, Azure, databases and Docker.

timeline.title: Reti S.p.A.
timeline.desc: My first professional role: building Angular pages, components and API integrations, and learning how frontend work gets done in a real team.

timeline.title: Gruppo Maggioli + Hinge 16
timeline.desc: Drupal and PHP on a public administration portal at Maggioli, then .NET, Blazor MAUI, Vue and WordPress for Hinge 16's clients, from long-term maintenance to sites delivered on my own.

timeline.title: Started building Crew
timeline.desc: Started Crew as an independent project, and with it began owning a whole product end to end: design, app, backend, web and cloud.

timeline.title: Crew released
timeline.desc: Released Crew on Google Play and the App Store.

story.text: It all started with a computer class in my last year of high school.
From the very first lesson, I wanted to understand how the software I used every day was actually built.
I learned by building things myself, one layer at a time.
First the page, then the data behind it, then the server that runs it.
Then came real teams and real clients.

I trained as a cloud developer at ITS Incom, then worked on Angular, Drupal, .NET, Vue and WordPress projects, from a public administration portal to client websites, mostly improving systems that people already relied on.
was the first product I built entirely on my own.
Product decisions, the Flutter app, the .NET backend, payments, cloud and store releases: every part of it was mine to work out.
What I enjoy most is owning a product as a whole, not just one layer of it.

projects.name: Crew
projects.description: Crew is an app for sharing your interests and making plans around them: post what you've been up to, explore posts and events on the map, then join an event or start one of your own — at a meeting spot or along a route with a few stops — and use the group chat to sort out the details. I built the whole thing myself, from the app and backend to payments, cloud and releases.

A post in Crew: golden hour at Tower Bridge, with its photo, place and comments
A host profile in Crew: Maya Chen's events, with Follow and Message

badge.text: Live on Google Play & App Store

story.title: Behind the build
story.imageAlt: Crew: Interests & Meetups on the App Store
story.body: Crew is the project that pushed me out of neat frontend/backend boxes. Building it on my own means I get to make the product and engineering decisions together — from small interaction details and geospatial data to payments, infrastructure and app store releases.

projects.name: TradePilot 212
projects.description: TradePilot 212 is a self-hosted MCP app that connects a Trading 212 account to ChatGPT and Claude: a portfolio dashboard, analytics, rebalancing, price alerts and order preparation right in the chat. Demo and Live stay separate, and every Live order waits for an explicit confirmation.

screens.alt: TradePilot 212 in a chat: the portfolio dashboard of a sample Demo account
TradePilot 212 in a chat: an order draft to buy Apple with a limit price, ready to review
TradePilot 212 in a chat: portfolio performance with profit and returns

projects.name: DevMate
projects.description: DevMate is a local-first MCP runtime I built so ChatGPT can work with the projects and tools on my machine instead of pasted snippets. It connects ChatGPT and Claude to VS Code, Obsidian, the CLI and local coding agents such as Codex and Claude Code.

images.alt: The DevMate workbench showing a project's uncommitted changes and their diff
DevMate handing a task to a local agent: Codex, Claude, Gemini or Grok, each in its own session

interlude.title: Sometimes, I zoom out.
interlude.description: The best decisions rarely come from staring harder at the screen. They come from stepping back — seeing how one small choice ripples through a whole system, and remembering the person on the other end of it.
interlude.returnTitle: Then I bring it back down.
interlude.returnDescription: Good solutions don't ask for attention. They just work — quietly and effectively.
